human_owner.summary: Approved in advance by the owner through auto mode; the Claude reviewer decides.

non_blocking_findings.finding: The source text pairs the right elbow with the left knee but also says the left knee goes toward the left shoulder. The frame shows a cross-body diagonal and the authoring response resolved this correctly. The instruction text is internally inconsistent.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Keep the cross-body diagonal assumption and note the source text inconsistency in the authoring notes.

non_blocking_findings.finding: pelvic_alignment adds low-coefficient gluteus maximus (0.21) and longissimus thoracis (0.105) as stabilizers. This is only loosely plausible for a crunch, since the pelvis stays mostly passive. The effect is small and does not change the main muscle pattern.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Optionally review whether pelvic_alignment is needed at all, since the rectus abdominis and obliques already carry the pelvic and trunk work.

non_blocking_findings.finding: The hip and knee flexion assists bring in hamstrings, gastrocnemius heads, plantaris and popliteus as low synergists. This follows from how the tracer maps knee flexion and is not a definition error. It also treats the knee bend as a trunk-linked action, though the support leg stays mostly flat.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: No change required. If revised later, keep the hip and knee flexion actions at assist emphasis.

non_blocking_findings.finding: The families trunk_flexion, core_rotation and hip_flexion are reasonable. hip_flexion is secondary here, since the leg only accompanies the trunk curl.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Optionally drop hip_flexion and keep trunk_flexion and core_rotation.

model_reviewer.summary: The definition fits the source and frames. The alternating cross-body crunch is modeled as bilateral trunk flexion plus rotation (primary), with assist-level hip and knee flexion for the drawn-in leg. The tracer output is a plausible pattern: rectus abdominis and both obliques are primary, hip flexors and hamstrings are low-level synergists, and a few low-coefficient stabilizers appear. The frames show a supine setup, hands behind the head, and the elbow meeting the opposite knee, which supports the identity, laterality and kinetic-chain label. Remaining concerns are minor and non-blocking.
